reason: The cited evidence (E1–E3) describes general durability testing and surface oxidation effects in related high-entropy alloys, but none provides specific data on reversible Os/Ir oxidation–reduction cycling, its correlation with ethanol oxidation durability, or in situ XANES/EXAFS tracking of these sites. The key premises thus lack direct prior support.
premises: Os and Ir sites in the alloy undergo reversible oxidation–reduction cycling under anodic potential holds
Moderate surface oxidation of Os/Ir transiently alters binding properties and enhances durability
Excessive oxidation leads to irreversible deactivation
Extended anodic holds increase the fraction of oxidized Os/Ir species observable by in situ XANES/EXAFS
Durability differences arise from oxidation-state modulation rather than physical degradation
